SPECIFICATION FOR LIPSALVE
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 September 1982, after the draft finalized by the Cosmetics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 Lipsalve consists of a homogeneous suspension of ingredients which It is useful in protecting the lips are petroleum or vegetable oil based. against chapping and cracking in extremes of temperature by forming a thin protective layer. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements which are petroleum or vegetable oil based. for lipsalves (lip balm )

1.2 Emulsion types, either oil-in-water or water-in-oil are not included. This standard also does not cover, lipsalves which contain ingredients that have an effect on the physiological functions of the body or lips for are made and also lipsticks or which specific therapeutic claims lipgloss. 2. TYPES 2.1 The material unctuous form: Type lshall be of the following three types in the stick or

The material shall be based on petrolem products, such as white petroleum jelly, microcrystalline wax, liquid paraffin, etc.

APPENDIX ( Clause 3.4 )
METHODS A-l. A-l.1 DETERMINATION Procedure OF TEST

A
FOR LIPSALVE RANGE ( POINT )

OF MELTING

A-1.1.1 Melt a quantity of the sample slowly while stirring until it reaches a temperature of 90 to 92�C. Remove the source of heat and allow the molten sample to cool to a temperature of 8 to 10�C above the expected melting point. Chill the bulb of a thermometer ( range 1 to 100�C ) to 5"C, wipe it dry and while it is still cold, dip it into the molten sample so that approximately half of the bulb is submerged. Withdraw it immediately and hold it vertically away from heat until the wax surface dulls, then dip it for five minutes into a water-bath having a temperature not higher than 16�C.
A-1.1.2 Fix the thermometer prepared in A-1.1.1 securely in a testtube so that its lowest tip is about 15 mm above the bottom of the testtube. Suspend the test-tube in a water-bath adjusted to 16�C and raise the temperature of the bath at a rate of 2�C per minute; up to 30�C. After the temperature of the bath has reached 30�C adjust the rate of rise to 1�C per minute and note the temperature at which the first drop of the melted sample leaves the thermometer. Repeat the determination twice on a freshly melted portion of the sample. If the variation in three determinations is less than 1�C take the average of the three as the melting point. `If the variation in the three determinations is more than 1�C make two additional determinations and take the average of the five. Report whether the average of the five determinations is within the range specified or not. A-2. DETERMINATION OF CONSISTENCY - Determination the penetration of consistency of the of a standard cone at

A-2.0 Outline of the Method material is made by measuring 25-O f 0.5%.

A-2.1 Apparatus A-2.1.1 Penetrometer - Any suitable penetrometer which permits the specified cone to drop vertically without appreciable friction for at least 40 mm and which indicates accurately the depth of penetration to the nearest 0.1 mm. The instrument shall have a table to carry the test
7

IS:10284-1982 sample, which may be adjusted to the horizontal before making the test. A mechanism for releasing and clamping the loaded cone shall be provided. A-2.1.2 ConeConsisting of a conical body of brass or corrosion resistant steel with detachable hardened steel tip, constructed to conform to the dimensions and tolerances shown in Fig. 1. The total moving mass, namely, that of the cone and its movable attachments, shall be 150-O -J= 0.1 g. The attachments consist of a rigid shaft having a suitable device at its lower end for engaging the cone. The outer surface should be polished to a very smooth finish. A-2.1.3 Constant Temperature Bath - A water-bath capable of regulation at 25% f 0*5?C and of suitable design for conveniently bringing the sample container to the test temperature. The bath should be provided with a cover to maintain the temperature of the air above the sample at 25�C. A-2.1.4 Timing Device - A stop-watch or other suitable instrument capable of measuring an interval of 5 seconds to within 0.2 second. A-2.1.5 Samfde Container - Flat-bottomed, metal or glass cylinders that are 100 & 6 mm in diameter and not less than 60 mm in height. A-2.2 Procedure - Melt a quantity of the sample at 82.0 k 2*5"C, pour into one or more of the sample containers, filling to within 6 mm of the brim. Cool at 25.0 & 2.5% over a period of not less than 16 hours protecting from draughts. Two hours before the test, place the containers in a water-bath at 25.0 + 0.5%. If the room temperature is below 23.5% or above 26_5"C, adjust the temperature of the cone to 25.0 & 0 5�C by placing it in the water-bath. A-2.2.1 Without disturbing the surface of the sample, place the container on the penetrometer table, and lower the cone until the tip just touches the top surface of the sample at a spot 25 to 38 mm from the edge of the container. Adjust the zero setting and quickly release the plunger, then hold it free for 5 seconds. Secure the plunger, and read the Make 3 or more trials each so spaced total penetration from the scale. that there is no overlapping of the areas of penetration. Where the penetration exceeds 20 mm use a separate container of the sample for each Read the penetration to the nearest 0.1 mm. Calculate the average trial. of the three or more readings, and conduct further trials to a total of 10 if the individual results differ from the average by more than f 3 percent. A-2.3 Calculation Consistency where A = mean of all the values of penetration 8 in mm. = +j-

A-5.2 Procedure A-5.2.1 Preparation of Sample - Weigh 2.000 g of the sample in a Kjeldahl flask of 500-ml capacity. Add 15 ml of concentrated sulphuric Heat cautiously. Add acid followed by 4 ml of concentrated nitric acid. drop by drop more nitric acid, if required, from a pipette to speed up the oxidation of the sample. The total amount of nitric acid shall be noted for use in the control test. When oxidation is complete, the solution is clear and faint yellow; at that stage, add 20 ml of water and again boil to fuming. Ensure removal of all nitric acid.

( Puge 3, clause 0.2 ) - Insert `the following new clause after 0.2 and renumber the subsequent clause:
`0.3 A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as EC0 Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), Government of India. The EC0 Mark is being administered by the Bureau ofldiun S~undurds Act, 1986 as per the Resolution No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 768 dated 24 August 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with EC0 logo, it shall also carry the Standard Mark of BIS besides meeting additional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS would be a single mark being a combination of the BIS monogram @ and the EC0 logo. Requirements for EC0 friendliness will be additional, manufacturing units will be free to opt for Standard Mark alone also. This amendment is based on the Gazette Notification No. 170 dated 18 May 19% for lipsalve as environment friendly products published in the Gazette of the Government of India. This amendment is, therefore, being issued to this standard to include environment friendly requirements for lipsalve.' ( Page 10, clause A-3) -- Substitute the following for the existing `A-3 TEST FOR PEROXIDE VALUE A-3.1 Reagenta A-3.LI Glacial Acetic Acid A-3.L2 Chloroform A-3.1.3 Potassium Iodide Solution -- saturated, freshly prepared. A-3.L4 Standard Sodium Thiostdphate Solution -- 0.01 N, freshly standardized. A-3.1.5 Starch Indicatwn Solution
#

Triturate 5 g of starch and 0.01 g of mercuric iodde with 30 ml of cold water and slowly pour it with stirring into one Iitre of boiling water. Boil for 3 minutes. Allow to cool and decant off.the supernatant clear liquid.

Amend No. 3 to IS 10284:1982 A-3.2 Procedure Weigh accurately about 5 g of the material in a 250-ml glass stoppered conical flask and dissolve by shaking in 30 ml of a mixed solvent containing 3 parts by volume of glacial acetic acid and 2 parts by volume of chloroform. Add 0.5 ml of freshly prepared saturated potassium iodide solution. Shake and after 2 minutes with occasional shaking, add 30 ml of water and titrate with standard sodium thiosulphate solution. Add the thiosulphate solution until the CO1OW of the titmted solution becomes light yellow. Then add 1 ml of starch indicator solution and continue the titration till the disappearance of the blue colour. Carry out a blank determination without using the sample. A-3.3 Calculation 1000 (V1-VZ) N Peroxide value mini - equivalentsdl 000 g =

M = massing of the sample taken for the test.
